content: A wart is typically a small, rough growth or tumor that often appears on the hands and feet. It may resemble the appearance of a cauliflower or a solid blister. Warts are caused by a viral infection, specifically by the human papillomavirus (HPV), and they are contagious through direct skin contact with an infected individual. Additionally, warts can be transmitted indirectly through shared objects, such as towels. While warts often resolve spontaneously within a few months, they can persist for years and may recur. Certain strains of HPV are also associated with the development of cervical cancer. The classic presentation of a wart is a raised, round, or oval lesion on the skin with a rough texture. Compared to the surrounding normal skin, warts may appear lighter, darker, or, in rare cases, black. Most adults are familiar with the typical appearance of warts and can easily identify them. However, atypical warts, such as those with smooth surfaces or flat warts commonly seen in children, may be more challenging for non-medical individuals to recognize. Some warts resolve without medical intervention, although this process can take several years. Regardless of treatment, warts that disappear may reappear over time. Warts are capable of spreading from one area of the body to another. For warts that are cosmetically unappealing or cause discomfort, treatment options are available. However, warts located around or beneath the nails are particularly difficult to treat compared to those in other areas. To reduce the risk of infection, it is advisable to avoid direct skin contact with warts on another person.
